item.title: Brazil President Lula Rides Trump Backlash to Cusp of History
item.description: The president’s odds of reelection are more than 60% in betting markets, but Brazil remains polarized and voters unpredictable.
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias

item.title: China Says Trump’s Economic Warfare Won’t Solve Iran Crisis
item.description: China said President Donald Trump’s threat to launch “economic warfare” on Iran and its trading partners wouldn’t work, urging cool heads to prevail.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Brazil Election: Lula Seen as Frontrunner Over Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A year after his popularity sank to career lows, Lula is a reelection favorite thanks to help from two right-wing nemeses: Donald Trump and Jair Bolsonaro.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Vinicius Andrade

item.title: Trump’s Aircraft Carrier Order Will Raise Costs, Contractor Says
item.description: President Donald Trump wants to switch the warplane launch systems on new US aircraft carriers. The company that builds those systems is suggesting that might not be a good idea.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Taiwan Cabinet Approves Record $35.1 Billion for Defense in 2027
item.description: Taiwan’s cabinet approved a record NT$1.12 trillion ($35.1 billion) defense budget for next year, highlighting its push to deter China militarily.
item.dc:creator: Miaojung Lin

item.title: What Bessent's US Treasury Intervention Means for Stocks & Mortgages | Daybreak Europe 8/20/2026
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
With a slew of unexpected maneuvers this year, Scott Bessent has emerged as the most interventionist Treasury secretary in financial markets in decades — putting his credibility on the line in an effort to quell a potentially damaging rise in US borrowing costs.
President Donald Trump announced plans to inflict what he called an “economic D-Day” against Iran, underscoring his frustration with the country’s refusal to capitulate despite weeks of strikes and a US blockade that’s crimped its oil exports.
And Bloomberg understands Banca Monte dei Paschi's board of directors is set to review strategic alternatives to Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover bid. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zambia Ex-Minister Killed In Raid on Opposition Chief’s Home
item.description: Zambian police said a former transport minister was killed in a raid at the main opposition leader’s house last week, a day after elections that were tainted by claims of irregularities.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill and Taonga Mitimingi

item.title: Russian Strikes Leave Ukraine Farmers With Piles of Unsold Grain
item.description: More than four years ago, Ravil Dzhamally fled his farm in Ukraine’s Kherson region after it was overrun by invading Russian troops. When Moscow’s forces were driven back, he returned to clear his fields of mines and plant wheat, barley and sunflowers.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Stasiuk

item.title: Pakistan Blasts US Envoy’s Remark About Disputed Kashmir Region
item.description: Pakistan condemned a statement by the American ambassador in New Delhi that referred to a disputed territory as an “important part of India,” underscoring tensions between the nations over Jammu and Kashmir.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra

item.title: Will Trump and Kim Jong Un Meet? Why US Is Seeking to Reengage With North Korea
item.description: US President Donald Trump is hoping to meet Kim Jong Un this year and says the North Korean leader has responded to a request to talk. North Korea has denied there’s been any direct communication and appears unmoved by Trump’s overtures.
item.dc:creator: Denny Thomas

item.title: China Tests a New Maritime Presence East of Taiwan, Report Says
item.description: China is responding to closer cooperation between the Philippines and Japan by expanding its presence east of Taiwan in an apparent bid to establish jurisdiction over waters in the Philippine Sea, according to the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: North Korea Fires Missiles After Dismissing Trump Overtures
item.description: North Korea fired a barrage of short-range ballistic missiles on Thursday, a day after it dismissed US President Donald Trump’s overtures to revive dialogue.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi and Sarah Hilton

item.title: UK Signals Tougher Stance on Israel With Sanctions Threat
item.description: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the British government would prepare targeted sanctions against Israelis participating in “illegal settlement expansion” in Gaza and the West Bank, in the latest sign of Labour’s hardening stance toward the Middle East nation.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Democratic Socialist Wins Upset in FL Senate Primary | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/19/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia says he opposes more data centers in his district, arguing that development has created power and environmental problems and driven up some residents' utility bills. Jason Furman, former Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers under President Obama, says higher interest rates are "likely here to stay" as government and businesses compete for capital, with US national debt surpassing $40 trillion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says US Is Waging Economic Warfare Against Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump threatened Iran and its trading partners with economic isolation after months of military strikes and a maritime blockade failed to force Tehran to capitulate.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank and Patrick Sykes

item.title: Higher Interest Rates Are 'Likely Here to Stay': Furman
item.description: Jason Furman, former Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers under President Obama, says higher interest rates are "likely here to stay" as government and businesses compete for capital, with US national debt surpassing $40 trillion. Furman says Congress ultimately must address the fiscal imbalance through spending cuts, tax increases, or both. He also weighs in on the economic impact of AI, arguing meaningful productivity gains may still be one to three years away as businesses learn how to deploy the technology. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Subramanyam: Data Centers Need Community Buy-In
item.description: Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia says he opposes more data centers in his district, arguing that development has created power and environmental problems and driven up some residents' utility bills. Subramanyam calls for a national strategy to site data centers where sufficient power can be provided without negatively affecting surrounding communities and expresses skepticism about "bring your own power" proposals that rely on diesel backup generators. He says the US should remain a leader in AI, but communities should not have to shoulder the costs of the infrastructure needed to power it. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Minutes Released as Yields Continue Climb | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/19/2026
item.description: Bloomberg TV & Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee breaks down the minutes from the July Fed meeting, where the board splintered on whether or not to raise interest rates. BlackRock Head of US iShares Fixed Income Strategy Karen Veraa-Perry also joins Businessweek to react to headlines from the minutes. Plus, President Trump held a meeting Wednesday at the White House with top Crypto leaders. Bloomberg News Senior Executive Editor stacy-marie ishmael, White House Correspondent Jeff Mason, and Bloomberg Government Senior Capitol Hill Reporter Cristiano Lima-Strong preview the event and what it means for the Trump Administration's crypto agenda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Set to Cut Tariffs on Canada Metals, Autos in Trade Deal
item.description: The tentative trade deal between the US and Canada would lower tariffs on certain Canadian exports of steel and aluminum to 25% and cut duties on Canadian auto exports to 15%, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Alicia Diaz and David Welch

item.title: North Korea Denies Kim Talks as Trump Eyes Meeting This Year
item.description: North Korea denied any direct communication between Kim Jong Un and President Donald Trump even as the US president said he’s seeking to meet with the strongman this year.
item.dc:creator: Se Young Lee and Tyler Kendall
